title: Identity & Access Management: Build vs Buy
question: Should our growth-stage startup build custom OAuth2/OIDC authentication in-house or purchase an enterprise solution like Auth0 / WorkOS?
description: Evaluates ongoing monthly SaaS seat costs and vendor lock-in against internal security maintenance, compliance certifications (SOC2/HIPAA), and MFA roadmap.
expectedConflict: Melchior models long-term compounding SaaS costs at scale; Balthasar stresses security liability and credential theft risk of custom cryptographic implementations; Casper recommends buying Auth0 for day one and planning abstraction wrappers.
keyTradeoffs: Immediate enterprise compliance readiness vs ongoing recurring per-MAU subscription cost
Core product focus vs diverting senior engineering hours to identity security
Complete custom user-flow flexibility vs standardized vendor identity schemas

title: Infrastructure Choice: Kubernetes vs Managed PaaS for a 5-Person Team
question: Should a 5-person engineering team adopt Kubernetes (EKS) for infrastructure parity or stick with a managed platform like Render / ECS / App Runner?
description: Evaluates future-proof infrastructure scaling and cloud portability against massive operational complexity, Helm/Kustomize maintenance, and control plane management.
expectedConflict: Melchior values declarative manifests and unified container topology; Balthasar objects to the extreme cognitive overhead distracting a tiny team from product-market fit; Casper recommends managed ECS or Render until team reaches 20 engineers.
keyTradeoffs: Cloud portability and granular resource optimization vs operational cognitive load
Ecosystem tooling breadth (Prometheus, Istio, cert-manager) vs setup velocity
Developer productivity on core product vs infrastructure plumbing toil

title: Code Review Policy: Mandatory Dual Approval vs Single Reviewer

Rigorous quality gates vs reviewer rubber-stamping fatigue
Centralized gatekeeper bottlenecks vs trust-and-verify decentralized velocity

title: Data Access Layer: Heavyweight ORM vs Type-Safe Query Builder
question: Should our new TypeScript backend use a heavyweight ORM like Prisma / TypeORM or a thin type-safe SQL query builder like Kysely / Slonik?
description: Evaluates rapid schema migrations and object abstraction against N+1 query surprises, complex JOIN performance, and raw database engine feature leverage.

keyTradeoffs: Developer productivity and object model ergonomics vs transparent SQL execution control

title: Release Strategy: Trunk-Based Feature Flags vs Long-Lived Release Branches
